---
title: "Scrape: minimum wage"
engine: knitr
---

The "List of countries by minimum wage" table has a nested header: the annual and hourly figures are each split into nominal and PPP sub-columns.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

`rvest` reads only the top header row, so the R version rebuilds the same names from the first data row.

```{r}
#| label: scrape-minimum-wage-r
#| eval: false
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

html <- request("https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_minimum_wage") |>
  req_user_agent("wikimill-project/0.1") |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_html()

tables <- html_table(html)
wage <- Filter(\(t) "Annual" %in% names(t), tables)[[1]]
# html_table() keeps only the top header row; the second one lands in row 1
names(wage) <- paste(names(wage), unlist(wage[1, ]), sep = "_")
wage <- wage[-1, ] |>
  mutate(across(matches("Nominal|PPP"), parse_number))
write_csv(wage, "data/minimum_wage.csv")
head(wage)
```

## Python

`pandas` reads this as a `MultiIndex`, so we flatten it into single column names before saving.

```{python}
#| label: scrape-minimum-wage-py
#| eval: false
import io
import pandas as pd
import requests

wage_html = requests.get(
    "https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_minimum_wage",
    headers={"User-Agent": "wikimill-project/0.1"}
).text
tables = pd.read_html(io.StringIO(wage_html), match="Minimum wage")
wage = tables[0]
wage.columns = ["_".join(c for c in col if "Unnamed" not in c).strip("_")
                for col in wage.columns.to_flat_index()]
wage.to_csv("data/minimum_wage.csv", index=False)
wage.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-tip}

## Which language should I use? 

**`pandas` has the edge**

* `pandas.read_html()` reads the two header rows as a `MultiIndex`, and its default `thousands=","` turns `4,637` into a number. 

* `rvest::html_table()` keeps only the top header row, so the second row lands in the data (and `Annual` and `Hourly` each appear twice), and the comma-grouped numbers stay as text. The R version pastes the first data row onto the names, drops it, then runs `parse_number()` on the wage columns.

:::

These chunks are shown for reference only (`eval: false`), so rendering the site doesn't hit Wikipedia. Run `Rscript src/scrape_minimum_wage.R` or `python src/scrape_minimum_wage.py` from the project root to refresh `data/minimum_wage.csv`.
